messages:
jordan_cust: Hi, hitting a 400 on /v1/rerank. Error: "ambiguous input: found both 'documents' and 'candidates' at top-level and inside items". Can someone confirm exact expected shape?

jordan_cust: Our product sends payloads that look like this (we adapted from old search):
```json
{
  "query": { "text": "climate policy summary" },
  "documents": [
    {
      "id": "doc-1",
      "passages": [ { "text": "..." } ],
      "candidates": [ { "text": "..." } ]
    }
  ]
}
```

jordan_cust: Seems like the API wants candidates as a flat list but we have nested candidates per doc. Returns 400 or sometimes returns zero scores.

maria_cs: thanks for the sample — that helps. Our rerank endpoint expects either a top-level "candidates" array (list of items to score) OR a top-level "documents" array when using the doc+passage mode, but not both mixed within nested objects. The SDKs flatten/validate differently.

ana: quick note: if you include a "query" object nested (e.g., "query": { "text": ... } ) the rerank endpoint expects the query to be a string at top-level named "query" or "q" depending on API version. Nested query objects are ignored which can lead to unexpected zero scores.

ana: best repro steps: 1) send the exact payload you pasted 2) set header X-RW-API-VERSION: 2024-11-01 3) observe 400 with message referencing both keys.

ryan_infra: also note payload size. If you flatten nested candidates you'll often exceed the candidate limit per request (512). If you hit that the service will either error or truncate silently depending on config. That can explain sudden zeroed scores when your UI only shows top results.

maria_cs: workaround that has worked for customers — transform your payload to one of these two canonical shapes:

1) flat candidates shape:
```json
{
  "query": "climate policy summary",
  "candidates": [
    { "id": "c1", "text": "...", "doc_id": "doc-1" },
    { "id": "c2", "text": "...", "doc_id": "doc-2" }
  ]
}
```

2) documents + passages shape (no per-doc "candidates"):
```json
{
  "query": "climate policy summary",
  "documents": [
    { "id": "doc-1", "passages": [ { "id": "p1", "text": "..." } ] }
  ]
}
```

maria_cs: If you need to preserve which doc a candidate came from, include a "doc_id" on each flat candidate as shown.

jordan_cust: ah got it — our migration left nested "candidates" inside docs. We'll try flattening and sending top-level "query" as a string. Thanks.

jordan_cust: quick question — is there a validation flag or header we can send to get a clear validation error before production? Right now we sometimes get a 200 with all zeros which is hard to catch.

ana: good ask — currently we have a feature flag that can be enabled per-account to run strict schema validation (returns 422 with details). I've asked eng to enable for your org id; tagging infra.

ryan_infra: confirmed — I've enabled "strict-rerank-validation" for org: redwood-test-42. Expect detailed errors on malformed shapes. Will expire in 7 days unless you request extension.

maria_cs: I'll keep this thread open while you test. If you still see zero scores after flattening and fixing query field, we'll escalate to backend to check whether older SDKs are coercing shapes. :thumbsup:

jordan_cust: trying now, thanks everyone :pray:

jordan_cust: update — flattening + using top-level string query fixed it. Scores look reasonable. Appreciate the fast help.

maria_cs: awesome — closing the loop. If you want, we can add a short note in the migration docs about nested candidates and the strict validation flag.

jordan_cust: please do, would have saved us a few hours.

maria_cs: filing quick doc note and linking to SDK upgrade PR.

maria_cs: marking this resolved but keeping strict validation enabled until you confirm it's safe to remove.

jordan_cust: confirmed, can remove in 24h if no regressions.
